reuse.why: Step 0 routes schedule-template, getUpcomingDates and getNextDate through a new getScheduleDate, but later steps implement the daily-skip and holiday checks beside it in getNextDate and getDatesInRange instead of inside it.

duplication.why: The non-working-day test (isWeekend || isHoliday) is written three times (closure in getScheduleDate, loop in getNextDate, filter in getDatesInRange) and the 'skipWeekend && !daily' flag is computed separately at two callers.

placement.why: Date rules live in shared/schedules.ts and the new handler sits next to getUpcomingDates in server/schedules/app.ts, but the daily-schedule rule is spread across callers rather than kept in the shared helper.

scope.why: Mostly focused on the four requests; keeping getDateWithSkippedWeekend as a thin wrapper and adding a separate getScheduleDateString adds surface without need.

maintainability.why: The weekend/holiday/daily rule is now decided in several places with different inputs (schedule-template never passes holidays, getUpcomingDates does not apply the daily skip), so a future rule change must be found and repeated at each caller.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts) and getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) decide the daily weekend/holiday skip themselves and call getScheduleDate with skipWeekend forced off for daily schedules.

disguised_duplication.where: The isWeekend || isHoliday check is reshaped as the isNonWorkingDay closure in getScheduleDate, a while-loop condition in getNextDate and a continue-filter in getDatesInRange; the daily override is restated as 'skipWeekend && !isDaily' / 'config.skipWeekend && !daily'.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduleDate gained a holidays parameter (plus a getScheduleDateString wrapper); the daily-schedule skip was not added to it, so getNextDate and getDatesInRange each re-implement it and pass a computed flag, while schedule-template.ts omits holidays and getUpcomingDates omits the daily rule.
